pure-announcement.rationale: It is an evergreen sales landing page rather than a launch, release note, or funding announcement, so this specific disqualifier does not fit even though the page is wholly promotional.

duplicate.rationale: Nothing in the nearest concepts (OSV, MCP notes, Agent Skills format, code knowledge graph) touches software licensing or desktop app distribution.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Its one substantive claim — Tauri's updater can authenticate against Keygen with a license header — is demonstrated in a snippet checkable against both projects' public docs.

durability.rationale: The page is customer logos, a Capterra star rating, pricing links, and 'free during development' copy; the sole technical content is one updater snippet bound to current Tauri and Keygen API details, leaving nothing that stays useful in twelve months.

actionability.rationale: Its only guidance is product-bound — call Keygen's licensing and distribution API and paste the updater snippet — which is a vendor onboarding step, not transferable build-or-decide knowledge.

atomicity.rationale: It says exactly one thing — license and auto-update a Tauri app through Keygen's API — so the core is trivially stateable in a paragraph.
